Subject: Dedicated throughput guarantees — what do you measure?

Soojin,

Thanks for taking the time yesterday. As we evaluate a Dedicated GPU pool with Redwood, procurement and engineering need clearer definitions on the throughput guarantees you would put in the SOW. A few concrete asks:

- Do you guarantee tokens/sec, requests/sec, or both at the pool level?
- How do you measure latency SLOs (p95/p99) — include warm vs cold cache behavior?
- What is the measurement window and repeatability requirement to validate the guarantee?
- How do guaranteed numbers map to discount tiers for reserved commits?

We plan to run a validation window with our traffic patterns but want to align on the protocol and telemetry access so we can independently verify. Please attach the measurement protocol and any sample tooling configs.

Priya
Priya Shah
Head of AI Platform, Acme ML

Subject: Re: Dedicated throughput guarantees — what do you measure?

Priya —

Great questions. I put together a short protocol and an initial commercial mapping (attached) but wanted to summarize the key points here so we can iterate quickly:

1) What we guarantee
- Primary guarantee: Pool-level sustained throughput measured in generated tokens/sec (tokens generated per second across the committed pool) and requests/sec as a secondary visibility metric. We treat the pool as a logical capacity (not an isolated GPU when customers buy a pool).
- Latency targets: p50/p95/p99 for end-to-end request-to-last-token. Typical offer: p95 <= 250ms for short prompts under committed throughput; p99 <= 750ms as a baseline for the same. Exact numbers depend on model family and sequence lengths — see attached protocol for model buckets.

2) Measurement methodology (high level)
- Acceptance test: three 30-minute steady-state windows run over two calendar days (six windows total). Each window is a steady-state synthetic workload that mirrors your prompt-length distribution. We compute tokens/sec and the latency percentiles over rolling 15-minute sub-windows; the guarantee is met if at least 5 of 6 windows meet thresholds.
- Cache consideration: We report both cold-start and warm-cache runs. Guarantees apply to warm-cache steady-state. Cold-start behavior is characterized separately and used for operational planning (we give expected transient spikes).
- What we log: per-request timestamps, prompt length, generated tokens, backend GPU id (redacted), batch size, and KV-cache hit ratio. You get sanitized telemetry export for the test window and a CSV of per-minute aggregates.

3) Discounts & reserved commits
- We propose discount tiers tied to committed vGPU-equivalent capacity (e.g., 4, 8, 16 vGPU pools) and the chosen guarantee level. Higher commits -> larger discount and stronger throughput SLAs. The attached spreadsheet maps commit tiers to discount % and the minimum guaranteed tokens/sec.

4) Credits and remediation
- If the pool-level guarantee is missed (per the acceptance protocol), credits are calculated as a percentage of monthly reserved fees proportional to the shortfall aggregated over the test windows. We also offer remediation runbooks and an option for a one-time capacity bump while we resolve.

I've attached: RDW-Dedicated-Throughput-Protocol-v1.pdf (protocol + sample tooling configs) and RDW-Commit-Tiers-and-Discounts-2026.xlsx. Aditya — can you add the technical test-harness notes (short) into the protocol doc?

Next step: if this looks acceptable, schedule a five-hour validation slot the week of May 25 and procurement can sign the MSA addendum that references the protocol.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Sr. Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Attachments: RDW-Dedicated-Throughput-Protocol-v1.pdf; RDW-Commit-Tiers-and-Discounts-2026.xlsx

Subject: Re: Dedicated throughput guarantees — technical measurement details

Priya — adding the engineering specifics you asked for so you can evaluate feasibility on your side. These are also in the test-harness file attached to the protocol.

Measurement definitions and notes:
- tokens/sec: measured as generated tokens per wall-clock second (excludes prompt tokens for the purposes of the guarantee). We report both prompt+generated and generated-only rates.
- requests/sec: raw API call rate accepted by the front-end. Note that batching can increase tokens/sec while reducing requests/sec; both metrics are reported.
- Latency: end-to-end includes queuing, decode, and streaming overhead. For streaming use cases we define latency as time-to-first-byte (TTFB) for the response plus time-to-last-token for completeness.

Synthetic workload profile (recommended for validation):
- Prompt length distribution: 60% short (<= 32 tokens), 30% medium (33-128 tokens), 10% long (>128 tokens).
- Generation target: fixed target lengths per bucket to isolate generation cost (e.g., short -> 64 tokens gen).
- Batching: continuous client with target batch window 10-40ms; runtime uses dynamic batching subject to SLOs.
- KV-cache: run warm-cache validation with a warm-up period of 10 minutes at 50% load and measure steady-state after warm-up. Also run one cold-start window (cache flushed) to profile spikes.

Repro tooling and CLI snippet (example):
- We recommend using k6 or wrk-style harness that can replay JSON bodies with variable tokens. The attached test-harness-sample.cfg is a k6-compatible config. A sample command: k6 run --vus 200 --duration 30m --summary-export=acme-window1.json test-harness-sample.cfg

Acceptance rule (engineering):
- Of six windows, at least five must meet the p95 and tokens/sec thresholds. If the pool misses thresholds due to a runtime bug on Redwood's side, we provide remediation credits and a post-mortem. If the miss is caused by customer traffic patterns outside the agreed profile, we provide operational guidance and may propose an alternate commit tier.

If you want, we can provide the harness as a runnable container in our test project so your infra team can run from your VPC.

— Aditya
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Soojin / team,

Thanks for the summary. A couple procurement points before we lock dates:

- We need the guarantee expressed at the pool level in the SOW (tokens/sec sustained over X minutes) and a clear, formulaic credit calculation. Can you provide SOW paragraph language we can insert directly?
- Will Redwood provide the telemetry export (CSV) for independent verification? We need the per-minute aggregates and per-request logs for the test windows. Please confirm retention and PII redaction.
- For discounts we prefer an objective mapping: e.g., commit of N vGPU => X% discount and Y tokens/sec minimum. The spreadsheet is a good start but we need those exact numbers in the SOW itself.

Procurement would also like to see the proposed credit table (0-5%/5-15%/15%+ of monthly fee) with examples.

If you can send a short SOW clause and the credit table I can circulate internally and then we can lock the validation window.

Regards,
ACME Procurement

Team —

Appreciate the clear asks. Attached is an excerpt you can drop into the MSA addendum (excerpt named: RDW-Dedicated-Throughput-Protocol-v1.pdf, section 3.1). Highlights:

- SOW clause (excerpt): "Redwood will provide a pool-level sustained throughput guarantee measured as generated tokens/sec across the committed pool. The guarantee shall be validated via the acceptance test protocol and telemetry exports described in RDW-Dedicated-Throughput-Protocol-v1. The minimum guaranteed tokens/sec and associated latency targets (p95/p99) for the customer’s chosen commit tier are enumerated in the commit tier table attached to the addendum."

- Credit calculation (summary): "If the minimum guaranteed tokens/sec is not met per the acceptance protocol, credit percentages are applied to the monthly reserved fee for the affected month. Credits scale with the shortfall magnitude and are capped at 50% for severe outages. Examples and exact percentage bands are in the attached spreadsheet."

- Telemetry: we will provide per-request logs (PII/redacted) and per-minute aggregates for the acceptance windows via a secure S3 export. Retention for acceptance artifacts is 90 days; production telemetry is configurable per your contract.

Commercial/next steps:
- Option A (baseline): 8-vGPU pool, 12% discount, guarantee: 18k generated tokens/sec pool-level p95 <= 250ms.
- Option B (premium): 16-vGPU pool, 18% discount, guarantee: 36k generated tokens/sec pool-level p95 <= 220ms.
- Option C (enterprise): custom commit, greater than 16 vGPU, bespoke discounts and SLAs.

If procurement likes Option A or B we will attach the commit tier line-item to the MSA addendum and schedule the validation windows. We can also do a joint run from your VPC with our harness.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a DocuSign link for the addendum and the calendar invites for the validation slots.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Sr. Account Executive — Redwood Inference
